newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 12.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Ex-president Choi Kyu-Hah will be compelled to testify November 14 during appeals trial involving mutiny and treason charges against former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo.
- Samsung Electronics develops 64-bit chip with processing speed twice as fast as Intel's P6S, the world's best existing microprocessor.
- Government to submit five labor law revision bills to the national assembly early next month.

- North Korea operates 10 opium farms to earn foreign currency, and is conducting massive military training in preparation for invasion of South Korea, a North Korean defector says at a press conference.
- Government enacts news energy tax to deregulate prices on petroleum products as part of a 10-year plan.
- Former president Choi, who has repeatedly refused to respond to a court summons, will be compelled to testify in appeals trial for two successors on mutiny and treason charges.
- Former president Choi ordered to take witness stand in the treason and mutiny appeals trial for ex-presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo.
